models_evaluated: machine learning algorithm estimating 5-year risk of six diabetes complications

links.outcome: Change in HbA1c, LDL-C, BMI quality indicators and therapy initiation, test vs control group
links.effect: Test group improved more than controls: HbA1c ≤7.0% +9.0% vs +4.5%; LDL-C <70 +27.9% vs +20.7%; BMI <25 +16.5% vs +11.0%; HbA1c >8.0% -18.4% vs -10.1%.
links.quote: Compared to controls, test group patients showed significantly greater improvements in HbA1c ≤7.0 % (+9.0 % vs. +4.5 %), LDL-C <70 mg/dL (+27.9 % vs. +20.7 %), and BMI <25 kg/m2 (+16.5 % vs. +11.0 %), with larger reductions in HbA1c >8.0 % (-18.4 % vs. -10.1 %).

screen.reason: The study evaluated the clinical impact of deploying an ML risk prediction tool directly into electronic medical records across 38 diabetes clinics, comparing outcomes of patients where the score was generated versus those where it was not.

primary.practice: EMR integration and clinical decision support risk alert generation
